document.title: Afghanistan: Taliban Said to Loosen Grip on Bin Ladin as They Increasingly Turn to Him for Financial Support and Advice (Islamabad 04450)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Haqqani History: Bin Ladin's Advocate Inside the Taliban
document.note: [Confidential] Sources say Jalaluddin Haqqani is an important advocate for Osama bin Laden within the Taliban administration. Bin Laden appears to operate largely free of Taliban control and to be protected by Taliban elements. His growing autonomy is attributed to the strength of supporters such as Haqqani, who are ideologically close to him and have argued for reducing controls on him.

sources_cited: Unnamed sources of US Embassy POLOFF meetings of 10-12 June 1998 (redacted)
key_claims: Taliban increasingly sought funds from bin Ladin in 1998 for arms, salaries and satellite phones/radios.
Bin Ladin's influence over the Taliban should not be overstated; he is not in their Afghan-only inner circle and is not much trusted.
Taliban may be loosening controls on bin Ladin as a quid pro quo for financial support.
Bin Ladin's supporters Jalaluddin Haqqani, Syed Abdullah (Haji Agha) and Abdul Kabir gained influence and argued for reducing restrictions on him.
Bin Ladin allegedly attended the Taliban inner shura in May 1998 and got approval for the Khost press conference; Taliban envoy denied prior knowledge.
The Taliban/bin Ladin relationship appears to be in flux and possibly growing closer.
